learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialization, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies, including notions of the latest advances.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to choose and apply relevant established analytical, computational, and experimental methods and to correctly interpret the results of these analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods; to recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to plan, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems in their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as to select and apply appropriate project methods.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations within their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Understand the objective and functioning of a mechanical assembly and correctly represent the parts of any assembly following representation standards.

teaching_methods: Lectures (teacher presentation in the classroom in participatory classes, covering concepts and procedures)
Workshop and/or laboratory practices (individually or in teams)
Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memoranda, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs (individually or in teams)

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, delivered documentation, technical presentation and defense
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed formative activities

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3 out of 10 must be obtained in the written test for outcomes RGM1011 and RGM1013 to calculate the final grade. The individual written test has a resit; its grade is calculated with 25% from the first control point and 75% from the resit. Projects and other assignments for all outcomes (RGM1011, RGM1012, RGM1013, RGM181, RGM182, RGM191, RGM192) do not have resit mechanisms.
